correctness.rationale: For each integer d>=w>=1, every affine parity hyperplane is conjugate to parity loss on Q_w tensored with a unitary idle cube. Walsh spectral weights 2^-w binom(w,j) give exact 2x2 survival decomposition; B*B kernel gives q_w and dark rank. The dissipative Lyapunov equation yields each finite-mode survival integral, hence the conditional-time formula and unique positive optimum. The local binomial central limit with a uniform bound gives the parity-dependent sharp constants. Separate numerical checks cover 1207 full-matrix/time comparisons, 220 independently solved Lyapunov equations, and dark ranks w=2..10. Numerical tests corroborate, not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result resolves a model-intrinsic comparison between detectors of identical macroscopic cardinality: the support parity alone can switch perfect to imperfect capture. It also gives full finite-time survival and a sharp unique physically tunable loss-rate optimum with distinct large-support constants, useful as a quantum-network trapping benchmark. The conditional-time objective is explicitly separated from overall success probability, and the result does not assert superiority among all detector subsets.
